problem: Given that $f(x)=5{e}^{x}+1$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=0.$

feedback.problem: Given that $f(x)=9{e}^{x}+ln⁡4$, the slope of the tangent line at $x=ln⁡2$ is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $ln⁡4$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

First, using the addition rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{e}^{x}+ln⁡4) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡4) \\  & =9\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+0 \\  & =9{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=ln⁡2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=ln⁡2} & ={(9{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=ln⁡2} \\  & =9{e}^{ln⁡2} \\  & =9\cdot 2 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
